key_insight: KANs can predict airfoil pressure distributions well and interpolate across Mach number and angle of attack, but in this study they were slightly outperformed by a well-tuned MLP and bested by a GNN only at the cost of longer training.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs offer a compact alternative that may reduce training cost while remaining competitive for subsonic and transonic pressure prediction.
method: Compared KANs against MLPs and graph neural networks (GNNs).
Trained surrogate models to predict surface pressure coefficients on airfoils.
Evaluated interpolation across Mach numbers and angles of attack.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KANs reconstruct the full pressure-coefficient distribution and generalize across conditions, but overall performance is marginally below a suitably trained MLP and below a GNN with longer training.
watch_item: KAN performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and can show training instabilities, so careful optimization is essential.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
